title: Three Mile Island accident
detail: Partial meltdown at Three Mile Island Unit 2 in Pennsylvania; at least 45% of the reactor core melted.

title: Chernobyl accident
detail: Explosion and fire destroy Chernobyl Unit 4 in Soviet Ukraine, releasing at least 5% of the core's radioactive material across Europe.

title: US–Russia HEU Purchase Agreement signed
detail: Russia agrees to downblend 500 tonnes of weapons-grade uranium, about 20,000 warheads' worth, into reactor fuel for US purchase over 20 years.

title: McArthur River mine floods
detail: Water inflow floods part of Cameco's McArthur River mine in Saskatchewan (18.7 million lb/yr capacity), delaying production restart by at least two months.

title: Cigar Lake mine floods
detail: A rockfall floods Cameco's Cigar Lake project under construction in Saskatchewan; its planned early-2008 start is delayed and capital costs rise.

title: Spot uranium hits record high
detail: Weekly spot indicators peak at $138/lb, up from $10.90 in May 2003, before the first fall in 51 months to $135 on 30 June.

title: Fukushima Daiichi accident
detail: Earthquake and tsunami lead to meltdowns of three reactor cores at Fukushima Daiichi, rated Level 7 on the international event scale.

title: Megatons to Megawatts programme ends
detail: Final shipment under the 1993 US–Russia deal arrives in Baltimore; USEC had bought over 14,000 tonnes of low-enriched uranium since 1995.

title: Japan restarts first reactor post-Fukushima
detail: Kyushu Electric begins restarting Sendai 1 (890 MWe), ending almost two years with no Japanese reactors operating.

title: Spot price hits cycle low
detail: Monthly spot uranium falls to $17.75/lb, down from $34.65 in January and the lowest since May 2004, according to the EIA.

title: Kazatomprom announces 10% production cut
detail: Kazakhstan's state producer cuts planned 2017 output by about 10%, more than 2,000 tU or roughly 3% of world production.

title: Cameco to suspend McArthur River
detail: Cameco says McArthur River and Key Lake will stop producing by end-January 2018 for an expected 10 months, citing oversupply and low prices.

title: US declines uranium import quotas
detail: President Trump declines the 25% domestic-supply quota sought in a January 2018 Section 232 petition and sets up a Nuclear Fuel Working Group.

title: COVID-19 suspends uranium mines
detail: Cameco suspends Cigar Lake in late March; Kazatomprom follows on 7 April, expecting 2020 output to fall by up to 4,000 tU.

title: Sprott Physical Uranium Trust launches
detail: Sprott completes its conversion of Uranium Participation Corp into a trust, which starts trading in Toronto; adds about US$600 million to Sprott's assets.

title: Spot price tops $50
detail: TradeTech's spot indicator reaches $50.50/lb, the first time above $50 since July 2012, as the Sprott trust buys physical uranium.

title: Russia invades Ukraine
detail: Invasion and sanctions on Russia unsettle nuclear fuel markets; spot reaches $58.30/lb by end-March, its highest since April 2011.

title: McArthur River resumes production
detail: Cameco packages first pounds at Key Lake after about four years of suspension; planned output of 15 million lb/yr by 2024.

title: Niger coup disrupts uranium exports
detail: Military takeover halts exports from Orano's SOMAÏR mine, Niger's only producing uranium operation, which yielded 2,020 tU in 2022.

title: COP28 pledge to triple nuclear
detail: At COP28 in Dubai, 22 countries sign a declaration to triple global nuclear energy capacity by 2050.

title: Kazatomprom warns on sulphuric acid
detail: Kazatomprom says acid shortages and construction delays may keep 2024 output below its target of 90% of subsoil-use levels; 2025 also at risk.

title: Spot peaks at $107/lb
detail: After topping $100/lb in January for the first time since August 2007, spot uranium reaches $107/lb in early February.

title: US bans Russian uranium imports
detail: Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act signed; ban effective 11 August 2024, waivers possible until 1 January 2028, unlocking $2.72 billion for domestic enrichment.

title: Kazatomprom lowers 2025 production guidance
detail: 2025 guidance cut to 25,000–26,500 tU (100% basis) from 30,500–31,500 tU, citing sulphuric acid uncertainty and construction delays.

title: Microsoft deal revives Three Mile Island
detail: Constellation signs a 20-year power agreement with Microsoft to restart the 837 MWe Three Mile Island Unit 1, renamed Crane Clean Energy Center.

title: Russia restricts enriched uranium exports
detail: Moscow imposes a temporary ban on enriched uranium exports to the United States, with exemptions for shipments under one-off licences.

title: Orano loses control of SOMAÏR
detail: Orano confirms Niger's authorities have taken operational control of SOMAÏR, in which it holds 63.4%, and are refusing to export production.

title: US orders target 400 GW nuclear
detail: Executive orders set a goal of raising US nuclear capacity from 100 GW to 400 GW by 2050 and seek more domestic enrichment.

title: Sprott trust raises US$200 million
detail: Sprott Physical Uranium Trust announces a US$200 million raise; TradeTech's weekly spot indicator jumps 12% to $77.50/lb by 20 June.

title: Niger moves to nationalise SOMAÏR
detail: Niger's government announces it will take over the SOMAÏR uranium venture co-owned with Orano since 1968; Orano contests the decision.

title: Kazatomprom plans lower 2026 output
detail: Kazatomprom cuts its 2026 nominal production level about 10%, from 32,777 tU to 29,697 tU (100% basis), roughly 5% of world primary supply.

title: WNA sees uranium demand doubling
detail: World Nuclear Fuel Report's reference case sees reactor uranium requirements rising from about 68,920 tU in 2025 to just over 150,000 tU in 2040.

title: US backs $80 billion Westinghouse build-out
detail: US government partners with Westinghouse owners Cameco and Brookfield to support at least $80 billion of new Westinghouse reactors in the United States.

title: Uranium added to US critical minerals
detail: The final 2025 US List of Critical Minerals names 60 minerals; uranium is among ten additions since the 2022 list.

title: No Section 232 tariffs on critical minerals
detail: A Section 232 proclamation on processed critical minerals, citing uranium among energy-sector inputs, orders trade negotiations rather than immediate tariffs; update due within 180 days.

title: Spot price back above $100
detail: TradeTech's daily spot indicator jumps $8.90 to $100.25/lb, first above $100 since early 2024, as the Sprott trust raises funds for purchases.

title: Japan restarts Kashiwazaki-Kariwa 6
detail: TEPCO's 1,356 MW unit, its first reactor to operate since 2011, restarts; Japan now has 15 operating reactors, according to the EIA.

title: Spot retreats to mid-$80s
detail: Month-end spot falls to $84.25/lb from $94.28 in January and $86.95 in February, per Cameco's published averages; futures sit at two-month lows.

title: NexGen Rook I construction licence issued
detail: Canada's nuclear regulator licenses NexGen to prepare the site and build the Rook I uranium mine and mill in Saskatchewan; operation needs separate approval.

title: Long-term price reaches $99/lb
detail: TradeTech's Long-Term Price Indicator hits $99.00/lb, its highest since the indicator began in 1996; it stood at $87.00 at end-2025.
